_what: Labels declared in ops/launchd/ that launchd is deliberately NOT holding.
_how: scripts/launchd_plists.py --assert-held fails on every declared label launchd is not holding UNLESS the label appears here with a reason. The reason is required and must be checkable by someone who was not there: cite the doc, the decision or the switch.
_why_json_not_yaml: This file is read by a script the docs run under the system python3, which has no PyYAML. The launchd declarations beside it are JSON for the same reason.

not_held.ai.hermes.ngrok: the ngrok tunnel is off on purpose -- scripts/process_audit.py says so in the grade_launchd comment, and nothing on this estate depends on a public tunnel today
not_held.com.prospector.consumer: runs on Fly on the same machine as the scheduler; it publishes, so it touches money -- docs/ENGINE_MIGRATION_PROGRAM.md:444
not_held.com.prospector.live-update: it exists to roll the prospector-live laptop checkout forward; on Fly a deploy is the update, so it dies at cutover -- docs/ENGINE_MIGRATION_PROGRAM.md:448. The operator's switch store/scheduler/NO_AUTO_UPDATE (created 2026-08-18) says the same thing.
not_held.com.prospector.scheduler: the engine runs on Fly (prospector-engine) since the 2026-08-18 cutover -- docs/ENGINE_MIGRATION_PROGRAM.md:443
not_held.com.prospector.watchdog: restarts a stalled tick, which is useless on a machine that is off; Fly's own restart policy owns this now -- docs/ENGINE_MIGRATION_PROGRAM.md:445 and EDGE-7 at :147
